title: Forgiveness & Reconciliation
subtitle: Four separate things, and only one is yours alone.
objectives: Separate forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences
Explain why forgiveness does not require the other person

cards.title: Four things, collapsed into one word
cards.text: "Forgive and forget" asks for four separate things at once, which is why it usually produces none of them. Separate them and each becomes possible.

cards.title: They are not the same
cards.text: Only the first one is entirely yours.
points: **Forgiveness**: letting go of your claim to pay them back.
**Reconciliation**: the relationship working again.
**Trust**: believing they will not do it again.
**Consequences**: what follows from what was done.

cards.title: Four different things one word gets used for
cards.text: Tap each one. The fifth button is why this matters.

question.text: Which one can you do without the other person agreeing?
question.explain: It is a decision you can make alone.

cards.title: Three things it frees you from
cards.text: People refuse to forgive because they think it means all four.
points: **You can forgive** and still not be close again.
**You can forgive** and still not trust yet.
**You can forgive** and still ask for consequences.
**Reconciliation takes two.** If they will not, that is not your failure.

question.text: Does forgiving someone remove the consequences of what they did?
question.explain: And asking for consequences is not revenge.

cards.title: Peter asked for a number
cards.text: The answer is designed to end the counting.
points: **Peter asked:** is seven times enough?
**Seven was already generous** by the standards of the day.
**The answer: seventy-seven times.**
**Some translations say seventy times seven.** Either way, stop counting.

cards.title: Joseph, thirteen years later
cards.text: He had the power to retaliate and the brothers knew it.
points: **"You meant evil against me, but God meant it for good."**
**He named the wrong.** He did not pretend it was fine.
**Then he fed them.**
**Naming it and releasing it** happen in the same sentence.

cards.title: Mended, and you can see where
cards.alt: A mended ceramic bowl with its cracks filled in bright gold so every repair line shows
cards.text: The break is not hidden. It is held, and the bowl works again.

question.text: Which of the four needs the other person?
question.explain: You cannot do it alone, and that is not your failure.

cards.title: Carrying it costs you the next round
cards.text: A fighter still angry about round two loses round three.
points: **The grudge takes attention** you need now.
**It is not a moral point.** It is a performance one.
**Resentment is a tax** you pay and they do not.
**Letting go is partly self-interest.** That is allowed.

cards.title: A repaired part is not a new part
cards.text: You can fix something properly and still watch it more closely than the rest.
points: **The repair is real.** It holds.
**You still check that joint first** next time.
**That is not distrust of the repair.**
**It is a record.** Records are allowed.

cards.title: Forgiveness is not a trust reset
cards.text: Two different systems, and games keep them separate on purpose.
points: **You can unmute someone** and still not party with them.
**Forgiving is immediate.** Trust is a record.
**A record is rebuilt by behaviour**, over time.
**Keeping them separate is wisdom**, not bitterness.

cards.title: Reconciliation needs the other chair filled
cards.alt: Two plain wooden chairs facing each other, both empty, in an otherwise bare room
cards.text: Forgiveness you can do alone. This one you cannot, and that is not your failure.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences are four things.
Forgiveness is yours alone; reconciliation takes two.
Matthew 18:22. Seventy-seven times, which means stop counting.
Joseph named the wrong and released it in the same sentence.

quiz.text: Which of the four takes two people?
quiz.explain: You cannot do it alone, and that is not your failure.
quiz.objective: Separate forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences

quiz.text: Which of the four is rebuilt over time by behaviour?
quiz.explain: Forgiving is immediate; trust is earned.
quiz.objective: Separate forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences

quiz.text: Forgiving someone removes the consequences of what they did.
quiz.explain: Asking for consequences is not revenge.
quiz.objective: Separate forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences

quiz.explain: Already generous by the standards of the day.
Or seventy times seven, depending on the translation.

quiz.text: The point of that number is to…
quiz.explain: A number so large it stops being a count.

quiz.text: Why can forgiveness be done alone?
options: It is your own decision to release a claim
quiz.explain: It does not need them to agree.
quiz.objective: Explain why forgiveness does not require the other person

quiz.text: In Genesis 50 Joseph said his brothers…
options: meant evil, but God meant it for good
quiz.explain: He named the wrong and released it together.
With the power to do otherwise.

quiz.text: Joseph's response shows that forgiveness does NOT require…
Why is resentment described as a tax?
options: You pay it and they do not
quiz.explain: It takes attention you need now.
quiz.objective: Explain why forgiveness does not require the other person

quiz.text: Keeping forgiveness and trust separate is…
quiz.objective: Separate forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 6 Devotion, and the most practically useful week in the subject. Forgiveness, reconciliation, trust and consequences are separated out, because collapsing them into "forgive and forget" is what makes forgiveness feel either impossible or dishonest. The separation frees three real things: he can forgive without being close again, without trusting yet, and without waiving consequences. Genesis 50 is the model because Joseph names the wrong and releases it in the same sentence rather than pretending it did not happen. Matthew 18:22 is given with the translation note, since both renderings appear and the point is identical.
discussion: Ask him to name the four and which is his alone.
Ask whether forgiving means trusting again.
Ask what Joseph actually said to his brothers.
Ask what resentment costs the person carrying it.
extension: Have him write the four words down and sort one real situation into them.
Have him find Genesis 50:20 and read it aloud.
misconceptions: "Forgiving means forgetting." It means releasing a claim.
"Forgiving means trusting again." Trust is rebuilt by behaviour.
"If we are not close again, I failed." Reconciliation takes two.
